sections.title: PART A · Section A: Reading. Answer in ONE word.

questions.q: In which state was Kalpana Chawla born?
Which organisation selected her as an astronaut?
What was the name of the space shuttle on her second mission?

sections.passage:
Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal, Haryana, in 1962. As a little girl she loved to watch aeroplanes flying over her town and often drew pictures of them. Her teachers remembered her as a curious student who asked many questions.
After studying aeronautical engineering in Chandigarh, she went to the United States for higher studies and earned a doctorate. In 1994 she was selected by NASA as an astronaut. In 1997 she became the first woman of Indian origin to go into space, travelling more than ten million kilometres around the earth.
In 2003 she flew on her second mission aboard the space shuttle Columbia. Sadly, on its return journey the shuttle broke apart just minutes before landing, and all seven crew members lost their lives.
Kalpana's life continues to inspire young people, especially girls from small towns. She showed that with hard work, courage and a big dream, nothing is impossible. Schools, hostels and even a satellite have been named after her.

sections.title: PART B · Section A: Reading. Find words from the passage.

questions.q: Find words from the passage that mean: (a) protect (b) expensive

sections.passage:
Honey bees are among the most useful insects on earth. A single colony can have up to fifty thousand bees, and every bee has a job. The queen lays eggs, the drones mate with the queen, and the worker bees — all female — collect nectar, make honey, clean the hive and guard it.
Bees are famous for honey, but their greatest service is pollination. As a bee moves from flower to flower, pollen sticks to its body and is carried to other flowers, helping plants form fruits and seeds. About one-third of the food we eat, including apples, almonds and many vegetables, depends on pollinators like bees.
Unfortunately bee populations are falling in many countries. The heavy use of pesticides, the loss of wild flowers, pollution and changes in climate are the main causes. Without bees, farmers would harvest much less, and food would become costly.
We can help by growing flowering plants, avoiding harmful chemicals in our gardens and buying honey from local beekeepers.

sections.title: Section B: Writing. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: You are Farhan of Class X. Write an article (150–200 words) on 'Junk Food and Our Health'. Clues: tasty and easily available — too much salt, sugar and fat — obesity and diseases — poor concentration — advertisements — healthy home food — role of parents and schools.
questions.answer: Points: title and by-line; introduction (popularity of burgers, chips, cold drinks); harmful effects — obesity, diabetes, heart problems, tooth decay, tiredness and poor concentration; why children choose it — taste, advertisements, convenience; solutions — fruits, home-cooked meals, healthy canteen menus, awareness by parents and schools; conclusion — 'we are what we eat'. 150–200 words.

or.q: You are Ritu. Write a report (150–200 words) for your school magazine on the 'Blood Donation Camp' organised by your school.
or.answer: Points: heading, by-line; date, venue and organisers (school with a hospital/Red Cross); inauguration by the chief guest; number of donors (teachers, parents, staff), medical check-up, refreshments and certificates; awareness talk on the importance of blood donation; conclusion on the success and appeal to donate regularly.

questions.q: You are Sunita of 10, Gandhi Nagar, Lucknow. Write a letter (about 100 words) to the Municipal Commissioner complaining about the garbage dumped near your colony.
questions.answer: Format: sender's address, date, The Municipal Commissioner with address, subject (Garbage dumped near Gandhi Nagar), 'Sir/Madam'. Body: heaps of garbage not cleared for weeks; foul smell, flies and mosquitoes; danger of diseases; request to clear it regularly and place dustbins. Closing 'Yours faithfully, Sunita'.

or.q: You are Ajay. Write an email (about 100 words) to your cousin describing the new school you have joined.
or.answer: Include: To, Subject (My new school); greeting; the building, classrooms, library and playground; friendly teachers and new friends; activities and clubs; how you feel; asking about his/her school; closing with your name.

sections.title: Section D: Literature. Answer in about 40 words.

questions.q: What moved the heart of the Iron Man of India, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel? What did he do? (Co-operate and Prosper)
questions.answer: The poor plight of the cattle farmers of Gujarat, who worked hard but remained poor and were exploited by middlemen, moved his heart. He decided to organise them into a co-operative to give them a steady income, and assigned the task to Tribhuvandas Patel, which led to the Amul Dairy.

or.q: Who were the three people involved in uplifting the cattle farmers? What were their contributions?
or.answer: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel dreamt of the farmers' prosperity and planned the co-operative. Tribhuvandas Patel united the farmers and started the co-operative dairy, removing middlemen. Dr Verghese Kurien set up the processing plant, built Amul into India's largest co-operative dairy, founded NDDB and Operation Flood and made India the largest milk producer.
